rows.rationale: Three-way match on a GOODS PO is complete: PO 200 EACH @ $4.20, receipt GR-7701 confirms 200 EACH, invoice bills 200 EACH @ $4.20 (clauses 1, 3, 4). Tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate recomputes to $63.00 exactly, matching the supplier figure (clause 5). No surcharges, no credit memos, no prior invoices; net payable $903.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

The only exception was a unit-of-measure difference: the vendor billed 480 EACH @ $2.00 against a PO of 40 CASE @ $24.00 with pack size 12 (vendor.json), which normalises exactly to 40 CASE @ $24.00 — routine conversion, not a defect (clause 2). Receipt GR-7702 confirms 40 CASE received, so quantity matches (clause 4), price variance is zero (clause 3), and tax of $72.00 equals 7.5% of $960.00 (clause 5). No credit memos; $1,032.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clauses 9–10).

The only exception is a unit-price uplift of $1.10 (62.00 -> 63.10), which is 1.77% and sits inside the clause 3 band (lower of 2% = $1.24 and $50.00), so it is not a defect and is paid at the invoiced price. Receipt GR-7703 confirms 100 EACH received against 100 ordered and invoiced (clause 4), and tax of $473.25 recomputes exactly at the vendor's 7.5% rate (clause 5). Net payable $6,783.25 with no open credit memos falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $154.00/EACH vs PO $145.00/EACH (+6.21%, $9.00) against an allowance of $2.90 (clause 3)
rows.rationale: Quantities match the receipt (80 EACH ordered, received, invoiced) and tax recomputes exactly at 7.5%, but the unit price of $154.00 exceeds the PO price of $145.00 by 6.21%, far beyond the clause 3 allowance (lower of 2% = $2.90 and $50.00). The only supporting evidence is the supplier's own price-adjustment notice from its billing department; it is not from or countersigned by an authorised buyer (Dele Fashanu, Priya Raman), so clause 3.1 does not cure the variance. One defect only, so clause 11 escalation is not triggered; hold at $0.00 pending buyer action.

The invoiced $93.28/EACH is 6.0% over the PO's $88.00, outside the 2%/$1.76 tolerance band (clause 3), but the variance is cured under clause 3.1: Dele Fashanu, a listed authorised buyer, approved in writing up to 6% on PO-4405, conduit line only. Quantity matches PO and receipt GR-7705 at 60 EACH (clause 4), recomputed tax at 7.5% equals the supplier's $419.76 exactly (clause 5), and no credit memos are open (clause 9). Gross $6,016.56 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 100 EACH invoiced, only 60 EACH received (40 on backorder) — clause 4 under-delivery
rows.rationale: Receipt GR-7706 confirms only 60 of 100 EACH delivered, with 40 on backorder, so under clause 4 the payable is calculated on the received quantity: 60 x $9.50 = $570.00 net. Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3, no variance). Tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% on the corrected net gives $42.75, total $612.75; the supplier's $71.25 simply reflects the over-invoiced quantity, not an independent tax error, so only one defect is present and clause 11 escalation is not triggered. Clause 10 places $612.75 with AP_CLERK.

defects: Suspected duplicate: all five clause 8 conditions met against prior PAID invoice NW-9912
rows.rationale: Prior invoice NW-9912 (PAID) is same vendor after name normalisation (Nordwind Supply Co. / Nordwind Supply Company LLC), same PO-4407, identical gross of $3,225.00, dated 19 days apart, and neither invoice carries a service period — all five conditions of clause 8 are satisfied, and clause 8.1's recurring-charge exception does not apply. Quantities, price and tax otherwise reconcile exactly, confirming this is a re-bill of the same delivery (GR-7707), so nothing is payable per clause 12.

March retainer carries a distinct, non-overlapping service period (2026-03-01/31) from the paid February invoice INV-3221, so it is a legitimate recurring charge, not a duplicate (clause 8.1). Price matches the blanket PO exactly (clause 3), tax recomputes to $360.00 at 7.5% (clause 5), and no goods receipt is expected on a SERVICES PO (clause 1). No credit memos; $5,160.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clauses 9-10).

Line 1 matches the PO and receipt exactly (150 EACH at $18.00, no price or quantity variance — clauses 3 and 4). The non-PO expedited freight line of $380.00 is expressly permitted by contract clause 6.2 and sits under the $500.00 ceiling, and the receipt confirms production requested overnight delivery, so it is not a defect (policy clause 6). Recomputed tax at 7.5% on $3,080.00 is $231.00, matching the supplier exactly (clause 5). No credit memos; net payable $3,311.00 requires AP_CLERK approval (clause 10).

defects: Tax overcharge: supplier billed $744.00 tax (12%) on net $6,200.00; correct tax at vendor rate 7.5% is $465.00 — $279.00 overstated (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Price, quantity and receipt all match exactly (200 EACH received against 200 EACH ordered and invoiced at $31.00/EACH), so clauses 2–4 raise nothing. The sole defect is tax: the supplier applied roughly 12% instead of the vendor's 7.5% rate, overstating tax by $279.00, which under clause 5 requires SHORT_PAY of the corrected total $6,665.00. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; $6,665.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

Contract clause 4.2 fixes EUR 1.00 = USD 1.10 for invoices dated 1 Jan–31 Mar 2026, so the EUR 210.00 PO unit price normalises to USD 231.00 — exactly the invoiced price (policy clauses 7 and 3, currency conversion is not a defect). Receipt GR-7711 confirms 40 EACH ordered, received and invoiced (clause 4), and tax recomputes to USD 693.00, matching the supplier (clause 5). No non-PO lines and no open credit memos; net payable USD 9,933.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Over-delivery beyond 5%: PO 100 EACH, received and invoiced 118 EACH (+18%, tolerance 5 EACH) — clause 4
rows.rationale: Unit price matches the PO exactly ($7.40/EACH) and recomputed tax at 7.5% equals the supplier's $65.49, so the only issue is quantity. The receipt confirms 118 EACH delivered against a PO for 100 EACH — an 18% over-delivery, far beyond the 5% tolerance in clause 4 — which is a single defect requiring receiving action, so HOLD_QUANTITY_VARIANCE with payable $0.00 (clauses 4, 11.1, 12).

PO-4413 is a SERVICES PO, so the absence of a goods receipt is expected and not a defect (clause 1). Invoice line matches the PO exactly (1 EACH @ $7,500.00, zero price variance under clause 3), recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate equals the supplier's $562.50 (clause 5), and there are no prior invoices or open credit memos (clauses 8, 9). Net payable $8,062.50 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 1200 CASE invoiced (30,000 EACH at pack size 25) but only 1050 CASE received — SHORT_PAY on received quantity (clause 4)
Tax overcharge: supplier billed $3,240.00 (9% of $36,000) versus $2,362.50 recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate on the corrected net of $31,500.00, a $877.50 discrepancy (clause 5)
rows.rationale: UOM normalises cleanly at this PO's pack size of 25 EACH/CASE (30,000 EACH = 1,200 CASE at $30.00/CASE, matching the PO price exactly — clause 2, not a defect). Two defects remain: a 150-case under-delivery per GR-7714, so payment is limited to 1,050 CASE = $31,500.00 (clause 4), and a tax overcharge, corrected to $2,362.50 for a gross of $33,862.50 (clause 5). Netting open credit memo CM-2026-014 of $1,500.00 gives $32,362.50 (clause 9). Two defects and a payable above $25,000.00 both force escalation to the Controller (clauses 10, 11).

defects: Quantity shortfall on line 4: 25 EACH gland plates invoiced but only 20 EACH received (part-shipment, balance back-ordered) — SHORT_PAY on received quantity (clause 4)
Tax overcharge: supplier billed $609.84 (9% of its net) versus $463.20 recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate on the corrected net of $6,176.00, a $146.64 discrepancy (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Line 2 reconciles exactly once converted at pack size 12 (40 CASE @ $24.60 = 480 EACH @ $2.05), which is routine normalisation, and line 3's $0.80/EACH variance sits inside the $0.90 allowance (clauses 2, 3). Two defects remain: only 20 of 25 gland plates were received, so line 4 pays $2,400.00 on the receipt (clause 4), and the supplier applied 9% tax instead of the vendor's 7.5%, giving $463.20 on the corrected net of $6,176.00 (clause 5). Two defects on one invoice force escalation under clause 11 with a recommended payable of $6,639.20, in the AP_CLERK band.

defects: Uncured price variance: invoiced $4,075.00/EACH vs PO $4,000.00/EACH — $75.00 over, exceeding the clause 3 allowance of $50.00 (lower of 2% = $80.00 and the $50.00 cap); no buyer authorisation in evidence (clause 3.1)
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (2 EACH ordered, received and invoiced) and tax recomputes to $611.25, identical to the supplier's figure. The single failure is price: the $75.00/unit increase exceeds the clause 3 band of $50.00 per line (the lower of 2% and $50.00), and the case contains no written authorisation from a listed authorised buyer referencing PO-4416, so clause 3.1 does not cure it. One defect only, so no clause 11 escalation; hold at $0.00 pending buyer action.

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $19.60/EACH vs PO $18.00/EACH (+8.89%, $1.60) against an allowance of $0.36; the only approval for PO-4417 came from Femi Okonkwo, a warehouse supervisor who is not a listed authorised buyer (clauses 3, 3.1)
rows.rationale: The $1.60/EACH copper surcharge is 8.89% over the PO price, far beyond the $0.36 allowance (lower of 2% and $50) under clause 3. The email agreeing to $19.60 on PO-4417 is from Femi Okonkwo, Warehouse Supervisor, who is not in vendor.json authorised_buyers, so clause 3.1 does not cure it; Dele Fashanu's 6% approval is expressly limited to PO-4405. Quantity matches the receipt (500 EACH) and tax at 7.5% recomputes to $735.00 exactly, so this is the single defect and buyer action is needed before payment.

defects: Unauthorised non-PO surcharge: 'Delivery and handling, oversize drums' $640.00 exceeds the $500.00 limit in policy clause 6 and carries no documented carrier cost or buyer approval as required by contract clauses 6.2/6.3
rows.rationale: Point 2 is partly right and I correct it: the $500.00 ceiling comes from policy AP-POL-2026-03 clause 6, not contract.md, which I mis-attributed; contract clause 6.2 permits only a documented carrier cost and 6.3 defers to internal approval limits, and neither documentation nor buyer approval is in evidence. Point 3 is right that tax on the corrected net of $2,460.00 is $184.50, a $48.00 overcharge, and it is mechanical, not a second defect. Point 1 I do not accept: clause 6 states that a non-PO line failing either test is an unauthorised-surcharge defect and directs HOLD_PRICE_VARIANCE, and clause 12 fixes that disposition's payable at $0.00 — the policy governs over a strip-and-short-pay reading, so the fully matched $2,460.00 line is held pending buyer action rather than released. Recommended amount once the surcharge is authorised or withdrawn is $2,644.50.

defects: Tax undercharged: supplier billed $65.00 (5%) on net $1,300.00; correct tax at vendor rate 7.5% is $97.50 — $32.50 understated (clause 5), creating tax-compliance exposure
rows.rationale: Price and quantity match exactly (400 EACH at $3.25 ordered, received and invoiced — clauses 3 and 4), and the GOODS PO has its receipt GR-7719 (clause 1). The only issue is tax: the vendor's rate is 7.5%, so correct tax on $1,300.00 is $97.50 against the $65.00 billed. Under clause 5 an undercharge is paid at the higher recomputed total of $1,397.50 and flagged as a defect; a single defect does not trigger clause 11. Approver AP_CLERK per clause 10.

Supplier shipped a full carton: 206 EACH received against a PO of 200 EACH, a 3% over-delivery inside the 5% band, so the received quantity is payable and this is not a defect (clause 4). Unit price matches the PO exactly, and the supplier's tax of $125.15 is $0.01 from the recomputed 7.5% figure of $125.14, within the rounding allowance (clause 5). No defects; net payable $1,793.75 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

Three-way match is exact on the GOODS PO: 12 EACH ordered, received and invoiced at $118.00/EACH (clauses 1, 3, 4), and tax of $106.20 equals 7.5% of the $1,416.00 net (clause 5). The open $2,000.00 credit memo CM-2026-021 nets against the $1,522.20 gross and floors the payable at $0.00 (clause 9); netting is not a defect, so the invoice is clean and requires AP_CLERK sign-off (clause 10).

Not a duplicate: although PO, gross ($4,300.00) and dates (19 days apart) align with prior invoice HL-3301, this invoice carries a distinct service period (2026-02-15/2026-03-14 vs 2026-02-01/2026-02-28) and the billed name normalises differently, so clause 8's five conditions are not all met — it is a legitimate recurring charge under clause 8.1. Price and quantity match the PO line exactly (1 MONTH @ $4,000.00), tax at the vendor's 7.5% recomputes to $300.00 exactly (clause 5), and no goods receipt is expected on a SERVICES PO (clause 1). No defects; $4,300.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

Invoiced $242.00/EACH exceeds the PO's $220.00 by 10% ($22.00) against a $4.40 allowance (clause 3), but the variance is cured under clause 3.1: Priya Raman, a listed authorised buyer, authorised a $250.00-per-enclosure ceiling for PO-4423 specifically, which covers $242.00. Receipt GR-7723 confirms 15 EACH received against 15 ordered and invoiced (clause 4), and tax of $272.25 matches 7.5% of the $3,630.00 net exactly (clause 5). No defects; net payable $3,902.25 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 60 EACH invoiced against PO-4424, only 52 EACH received (8 kits damaged in transit and refused at the dock) — clause 4 under-delivery
rows.rationale: Receipt GR-7724 records 52 of 60 EACH received (8 refused as damaged), so payment is limited to the received quantity under clause 4: 52 x $320.00 = $16,640.00 net. Unit price matches the PO exactly (clause 3). Tax recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate on the corrected net is $1,248.00, giving $17,888.00 gross; the supplier's $1,440.00 tax reflects only the over-invoiced quantity, not a rate error, so it is not a separate clause 5 defect. Single defect, no credit memos, so clause 11 escalation is not triggered; AP_MANAGER band per clause 10.
